content.title: COOKING {{MISTAKES}} THAT CANCEL OUT YOUR EFFORTS
facts: **Garlic** – Chopping right before cooking reduces its health benefits; let it sit for 10 minutes after cutting to allow beneficial compounds to form.
**Olive oil** – Heating extra virgin olive oil past its smoke point breaks down its **antioxidants**; use it raw or for low-heat cooking instead.
**Vegetables** – Boiling vegetables and tossing the water drains away **water-soluble vitamins** like vitamin C and B vitamins; steaming preserves far more.
**Tomatoes** – Eating them only raw limits **lycopene** absorption; cooking with a bit of oil actually increases how much your body can use.
**Rice** – Not rinsing rice before cooking leaves more surface starch and, depending on source, trace **arsenic**; rinsing reduces both.
**Chicken** – Washing raw chicken under the tap doesn't remove bacteria; it just splashes them around your kitchen, raising contamination risk.
**Spinach** – Eating large amounts only raw limits **iron and calcium** absorption due to oxalates; light cooking reduces this effect.
**Turmeric** – Adding it to food without **black pepper or fat** means most of its active compound passes through unused.
**Salads** – Using only fat-free dressing reduces absorption of **fat-soluble vitamins** (A, D, E, K) from the vegetables underneath.
**Meal prepping** – Storing hot food in sealed containers traps steam, encouraging bacterial growth; let food cool slightly before sealing.
